label: Third-Party Nominee Stays Out
detail: The Green Party's candidate never enters the race, so voters face only the two major nominees and the remaining minor candidates.
assumption: Voters who would have backed the third-party nominee redistribute to the other candidates or stay home, based on their stated preferences and closeness to each major party.
facts_text: The third-party nominee who had been seeking the presidency on a platform of consumer protection, environmental protection and campaign finance reform ended his bid earlier in the year and is not on the ballot.
No other candidate has taken up his campaign, and voters who might have supported him must choose among the remaining candidates or stay home.
research_questions: Where a left-leaning third-party candidate is absent, how do his would-be supporters split between the major-party candidates and abstention?
How did voters who backed minor-party candidates in 1996 behave when no such candidate was available?
How much of the 2000 third-party vote came from people who would not have voted otherwise?
source_text: Ralph Nader does not run in 2000.
